title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a scheme of characteristic p. Let C be the category of finite étale group schemes E over S killed by p. Equivalently, C is the category of locally constant étale sheaves of F_p-vector spaces of finite type, i.e. F_p-local systems. Let C' be the category of locally free O_S-modules M of finite type equipped with a Frobenius-linear isomorphism F_M : M^{(p)} = Frob_S^* M -> M. In modern terms these are 'unit-root F-modules' or 'étale φ-modules' over S.

The functor φ : C -> C' sends E to (E ⊗_{F_p} O_S, F_E ⊗ O_S). The NB explains where the Frobenius comes from: (E⊗O_S)^{(p)} ≅ E^{(p)}⊗O_S, and the relative Frobenius F_{E/S} : E -> E^{(p)} is an isomorphism because E is étale.

Proposition: φ is an equivalence of categories.

(a) Full faithfulness. Passing to internal Hom, this reduces to Γ(S,E) ≅ {x ∈ Γ(S, E⊗O_S) : F(x^{(p)}) = x}. By étale descent one may assume E is constant, then E = F_p. The claim then becomes exactness of the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 -> (Z/p)_S -> G_a -> G_a, with the last map x ↦ x^p − x. This holds by base change from F_p.

(b) Essential surjectivity. Given (M,F), it suffices to show it is locally of the required form. View M as a vector-bundle group scheme V(M) and consider the 'Lang/Artin–Schreier' map ℘(x) = F_M(x^{(p)}) − x. Its differential is −id, so ℘ is étale. It is surjective (smooth). Hence its kernel E is an étale group scheme killed by p.
- Finiteness: it suffices to show that the F_p-rank of E on geometric fibres is locally constant, namely equal to rk M.
- Isomorphism: that E⊗O_S -> M is an isomorphism can be checked fibre by fibre (Nakayama).

This reduces everything to the next page's lemma over an algebraically closed field k: E = M^{F=1} satisfies E⊗_{F_p} k ≅ M. This is the Lang–Dieudonné theorem on semilinear Frobenius-bijective maps.

The next page generalises to Z/p^n-local systems versus W_n(O_S)-modules with Frobenius, and to smooth schemes in W-modules. This is the dictionary later standard as Katz's equivalence between étale Z_p-local systems and unit-root F-crystals.
errors: Surjectivity of ℘ as an fppf/étale sheaf map is asserted, not proved. It follows from ℘ being étale with surjective fibre maps (Lang's theorem on geometric fibres), so this is a gap of exposition only.

The finiteness argument needs E -> S to be quasi-finite with constant fibre rank, and then needs E to be finite. Étale plus separated plus constant degree is used implicitly. The deduction 'étale with locally constant rank implies finite' needs E to be closed in V(M), which holds because it is a kernel. Fine, but unstated.

ideas.what: Equivalence between F_p-local systems (finite étale p-torsion group schemes) and locally free O_S-modules with Frobenius isomorphism, in char p
ideas.modern_name: Katz's equivalence: étale φ-modules / unit-root F-modules ↔ étale F_p-local systems (char-p Riemann–Hilbert at level 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms' (1973), Prop. 4.1.1, also SGA 7 exposé XXII. Roots in Lang, Dieudonné, Artin–Schreier.
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals; not in EGA/SGA as such to my knowledge

ideas.what: Proof via the Lang/Artin–Schreier isogeny ℘ = F∘(·)^{(p)} − id on the vector bundle, its étaleness, kernel as the local system
ideas.modern_name: Lang torsor / Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence for unit-root F-modules

ideas.what: Extension to Z/p^n via W_n(O_S)-modules and representability by smooth W-module schemes (next page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz 1973; Crew; later Emerton–Kisin / Bhatt–Lurie Riemann–Hilbert

missed.claim: Grothendieck had, apparently around 1966 in connection with the crystals letter to Tate, the full statement and essentially Katz's proof of the equivalence between F_p (and Z/p^n) local systems and Frobenius-unit modules. That is several years before Katz's 1973 published version. A priority/attribution detail rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: Proposition Le foncteur φ est une équivalence de catégories.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: History of the char-p Riemann–Hilbert correspondence (Katz, Emerton–Kisin, Bhatt–Lurie). It shows the origin lies in Grothendieck's crystalline program. Mathematically, nothing is new.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard result (Katz's equivalence) with a standard proof. Only of mild historical interest as possible early Grothendieck priority; dating of the notes is uncertain (1966 to after 1970).
transcription_corrections: 'fibre par fibre (génial)' should most likely read 'fibre par fibre (Nakayama)'.
'il suffit de prouver qu'il est de F_p-rang localement cst - ou de prouver qu'il est égal au rang de M': the 'on' should be 'ou'.
'épimorphisme lisse étale' is better read as an inserted 'lisse' above 'épimorphisme étale' (the author's correction).
